english.title: Adult invite child or young person to enter licensed family entertainment centre - Gambling Act 2005
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) invited a

(A)_[child]_
(B)_[young person]_

aged **(..SPECIFY AGE..) to enter part of premises, namely **(..SPECIFY PART OF PREMISES..), which were a licensed family entertainment centre, and

(C)_[he]_
(D)_[she]_

having entered that part of the premises had access to a Category C gaming machine and at the time when

(E)_[he]_
(F)_[she]_

was invited to enter, a Category C gaming machine was

(G)_[being used]_
(H)_[available for use]_
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 47(7) and 62(1) of the Gambling Act 2005.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
invited a child/young person
to enter part of premises that were part of licensed family entertainment centre AND
child/young person entering that part had access to Category C gaming machine AND
at the time of the invitation to enter such a gaming machine was being used/available for use

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) This offence wording applies to adults, aged 18 or over, only; for young persons see the offence wording GA05094/H8273.
(ii) Section 45 of the Gambling Act 2005 provides that "child" means an individual who is less than 16 years old, and "young person" means an individual aged 16 or 17.
(iii) Section 63 of the Gambling Act 2005 provides the defence of reasonable belief about a person's age.

other.penalty:
Fifty one weeks imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
12 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
